$comment: Normative data contracts for the Build Assistant. The BUILD BRIEF is the instruction; this file is the schema. It pins the catalog shapes, the five laws, the stage-versioned dimension contract, the reference fixture with expected solve output, and the release-gate definitions so any implementation can be checked against them.

laws.1: AI never emits a number. Every number reaching a user traces to a solver field id.
laws.2: solve(answer_set, catalog, schema) is a pure function: same inputs -> same output -> same hash. No I/O, randomness or model calls.
laws.3: Answer sets are append-only. Revisions create new versions; nothing is mutated.
laws.4: Partial re-solve does not exist. Any input change regenerates everything downstream.
laws.5: No document releases with a failing gate. There is no override flag.

dimension_contract.$comment: Section 2.3 — every dimension is a triple, never a scalar. A dimension in a step without a stage tag is a validation error.

fastener.rationale: Tool schedule is derived from this; it must say '7/64 brad point', not 'a drill bit'.

invariants: Stacked element finished heights sum to declared overall height, accounting for co-planar overlaps
Reveals symmetric on all declared sides unless asymmetry was requested
Carcass offset equals finished reveal plus allowance of the inset element
Every part length greater than zero after allowance application
Unsupported span of any finish-bearing panel below its flex threshold
Continuous backing exists behind the full width of every finish-bearing surface
Every part fits at least one stock size in at least one orientation

release_gates.gate_1_number_provenance: Every number in narrative prose matches a solver field id; an unmatched number blocks release.
release_gates.gate_3_visual: Rasterize and inspect; catches drawing labels/shapes past a canvas edge that overflow no container.

reference_fixture.$comment: Section 2.5 — the golden test. Solver must reproduce every value below from the seven inputs.

material_note.$comment: The brief prose seeds '3/4 birch plywood (actual 0.703)', but the reference fixture's numbers are computed at actual 0.75 (slab.carcass_thickness 2.25 = 3 * 0.75; plywood util 4084.75/4608 = 0.886). The golden test governs, so the coffee_table build path uses a 3/4 structural panel of actual 0.75; the 0.703 birch entry is retained for other paths.
